correctness.rationale: An all-negative edge sends the opposite of its burned neighbor color. In any entirely yellow arm the leaf is ignited. If the center ends yellow, no arm can be entirely yellow because its middle would burn green after the leaf ignition. With a green center first burning at round t, a wholly yellow arm whose middle is ignited requires its leaf ignition at exactly t; a wholly yellow arm whose middle is spread-colored requires its leaf ignition at exactly t+1. A single ignition per round permits at most two such arms, hence Y <= m+2. The explicit four-round legal schedule realizes equality for three distinct arms and all remaining arms. Direct labelled-state and orbit-state simulations and witness replay corroborate the sharp statement, but are not used as infinite proof.

The statement gives a sharp exact infinite family with genuine branching and a process-specific time-of-ignition obstruction, not an immediate reduction to path plurality. It shows branching once-subdivided stars can have plurality approaching half the vertex count, versus about two thirds for all-negative paths.
